newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Tribal rebel leaders fly to Dhaka for peace talks.
newsitem.headline: Tribal rebel leaders fly to Dhaka for peace talks.

text.p: Leaders of Shanti Bahini rebels arrived in Dhaka on Saturday for talks aimed at ending a 23-year insurgency over tribal demands for self-rule.

The five-member rebel team, heaed by Jyotirindra Budhipriya Larma, chief of Shanti Bahini's political wing, flew to Dhaka by a military helicopter from Dudukchhari, a remote Chittagong Hill Tracts village near the Indian border.
Security was tight at Dhaka's heliport, not far from Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina's office, where police drove away reporters and photographers.
"No one must try to approach the guests," shouted an air force officer. "Better you leave before being whisked away," one reporter quoted a government official as saying.
Larma was received by Abul Hasanat Abdullah, a senior leader of Hasina's Awami League and the member of parliament who will be heading the government side at the talks.
They left the heliport immediately and drove to a state guest house at the city's centre.
"The talks would start without delay," one official said. "The outcome would be known at a joint press briefing in the evening," he added.
It was the first time that Shanti Bahini was attending a meeting with the government outside the Hill Tracts.

"We are expecting good progress in the peace talks," one official, who declined to be identified, said on Friday. "That the Shanti Bahini has agreed to send its leaders to Dhaka for a dialogue itself is an encouraging sign," he said.
Previous meetings between the two sides have been held in the hill town of Khagrachhari.
The Shanti Bahini (Peace Force) has fought a bush war for autonomy in the 5,500 sq miles (14,200 sq km) of Hill Tracts, bordering India and Burma, since 1973.
They also want 300,000 Bengali-speaking settlers expelled from the area.
Officials say more than 8,500 rebels, soldiers and civilians have been killed in the insurgency, which has forced some 50,000 tribespeople to seek refuge in the northeast Indian state of Tripura.
